prompt: A JTable of invoice lines needs a running total. Complete addRow and recalculate so the labels show "Total: $9.00" (US locale, two decimals) and "3 rows" after any change.
explanation: DefaultTableModel stores every cell as an Object, so reading a quantity or a price means casting -- casting to Number rather than Integer or Double keeps the code working whichever numeric type the cell happens to hold. Pinning Locale.US on String.format guarantees a dot as the decimal separator regardless of the machine's regional settings. Keeping the arithmetic in recalculate, and calling it from addRow, means any other edit to the model can reuse the same method.
hints: model.addRow takes an Object[] -- the int and double are autoboxed for you.
Loop rows from 0 to model.getRowCount(), reading column 1 for the quantity and column 2 for the price.
String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "Total: $%.2f", sum) produces the exact text the tests expect.
